brief: Goldman TMT sales desk wrap covering three separate threads without a single connected thesis. Market tape: the Fed delivered the expected 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% but surprised hawkishly, with dots showing one more 2026 hike, no cuts in 2027, and higher inflation projections; equities closed lower despite an initial pre-FOMC rally. AI infrastructure and optical names outperformed (Optical +4.8%, LITE +10%) while software (-0.9%) and internet (-1.4%) lagged, as the tape rotated toward profitable AI infrastructure over speculative AI-productivity exposure. Oil fell 3%, reversing the prior day's gain on East-West pipeline headlines. Desk flow: asset managers were net sellers, hedge funds small net buyers of tech. EU Communacopia Day 2: telcos were stable-to-constructive, with Spain (TEF, Orange, Zegona) the clearest positive on rational pricing and consolidation optionality and Germany the main caution; media names (RELX, Prosus, JCD, Scout) sounded broadly constructive on AI monetisation and capital discipline. Separately, Nebius is raising on-demand GPU prices 17-21% from 1 October and Intel says it can meet only about half of CPU demand, both signalling tight AI compute supply.
